question: In the late 18th century, which Indian cities rose in importance as the Presidency cities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta ( Kolkata), Bombay( Mumbai) and Madras( Chennai)**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the late 18th century, the cities of Calcutta (Kolkata), Bombay (Mumbai), and Madras (Chennai) rose in importance as the Presidency cities of British India:
 
• These cities became the centres of British power in India.
 
• They were also the main centres of trade and economic activities for the English East India Company.
 
• The cities had a different layout from the older Indian towns, and their buildings were influenced by colonial architecture.
 
• Institutions were established to regulate economic activities and demonstrate British authority.
